pages.title: Debugging
pages.content:
As you progress and learn more advanced concepts in PHP, you'll inevitably make mistakes in your code. Some of these mistakes can be difficult to identify. This is where **debugging** becomes crucial. Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors in your code.

### What is a bug?

A **bug** is an error that causes a program to generate an unexpected output, which is different from the intended or expected output, or sometimes produces no output at all.

### Common Error Types:

- **CE - Compilation Error / Syntax Error**: These occur when the code violates PHP's syntax rules, preventing the program from running.
- **RE - Runtime Error**: These happen when the program crashes or behaves unexpectedly during execution.
- **WA - Wrong Answer / Logical Error**: The program runs without crashing, but the output is incorrect due to a logic flaw in the code.
- **TLE - Time Limit Exceeded**: The program takes too long to execute, usually in competitive programming or time-constrained environments.

We will explore each of these errors in detail and learn how to resolve them in the upcoming lessons.

pages.title: Compilation error (syntax error)
pages.content:
Let’s start with **Syntax Errors**.

When writing code in any programming language, you must follow its syntax rules. If the correct syntax is not followed, PHP will throw a **syntax error**.

#### Example:
In English, a sentence is completed with a full stop (`.`). Similarly, in PHP, we complete each statement with a **semicolon** (`;`).

The following is an example of a syntax error — can you spot why?

```php
$number = 19;
echo $number . PHP_EOL
```

pages.title: Runtime Error
pages.content:
Runtime Error: Generally caused by accessing a negative or unreachable index of a string or an array or dividing a number by 0.

```php
<?php
$arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; // array initialization
echo $arr[0]; // accessing first element of array it prints 1 
echo $arr[-1]; // negative position of array doesn't exist so it will give you runtime error
echo $arr[5]; // this position of array does not exist because position ranges from 0 to (length of array)-1
```

Currently we haven't learnt about arrays - you will encounter some of these cases when we cover our module on arrays.

pages.title: Logical Error or Wrong Answer (WA)
pages.content:
A logical error is an error in a program that occurs when the code compiles and runs without producing any error messages, but it does not produce the expected or desired output.  
Instead, it performs a different computation or provides incorrect results due to a flaw in the algorithm or logic of the program.  
Logical errors are the hardest to find in a program.  

Based on what you have learnt so far - you will encounter logical errors of the following types:
- Incorrect Conditions
- Incorrect Index
- Incorrect variable usage

practiceProblems.title: Mismatched Parenthesis
practiceProblems.description:
In PHP (and most programming languages), **parentheses** must be properly matched. For every opening bracket `(` `{` `[`, there must be a corresponding closing bracket `)` `}` `]` of the same type. If mismatched or missing, it will cause a **syntax error**.

#### Example:
If we try to use different types of opening and closing brackets, PHP will throw a syntax error.

```php
$a = (5 + 7 };  // incorrect due to mismatched parentheses
```

The opening bracket `(` does not match the closing bracket `}`.

#### Corrected Code:
```php
$a = (5 + 7);  // corrected parentheses
```

### Task

You are provided with a program that checks whether a number is **odd** or **even**. The code contains a syntax error. Your task is to **debug** the code and fix the problem.

practiceProblems.title: Incorrect Index
practiceProblems.description:
In PHP, strings use **zero-based indexing**, meaning the first character of a string is at index `0`. Often, forgetting this and using **one-based indexing** can result in a **logical error**, where the program doesn't give the expected output.

#### Example: Program to Print the Last Character of a String

```php
<?php
$n = intval(fgets(STDIN));  // Input length of the string

$s = trim(fgets(STDIN));  // Input string

echo $s[$n] . PHP_EOL;  // Wrong answer, as string uses zero-based indexing

echo $s[$n - 1] . PHP_EOL;  // Right answer (prints last character)
```

#### Explanation:
- The incorrect logic is using `$s[$n]` to access the last character, which is one index beyond the end of the string (since indexing starts at `0`).
- To correctly print the last character, you should use `$s[$n - 1]`, which accounts for zero-based indexing.

### Task

You are tasked with writing a program that:
1. Takes a string as input.
2. Prints the **1st**, **4th**, and **6th** characters of the string.

practiceProblems.title: Oneful Pair Check - Debug The Code
practiceProblems.description:
Chef defines a pair of positive integers $(a,b)$ to be a Oneful Pair, if $a+b+(a \cdot b) = 111$ 

For example, $(1,55)$ is a Oneful Pair, since $1+55+(1 \cdot 55)=56+55=111$.  

But $(1,56)$ is not a Oneful Pair, since $1+56+(1 \cdot 56) = 57+56=113$ not equal to $111$.  

Given two positive integers $a$ and $b$, output Yes if they are a Oneful Pair. And No otherwise.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Chef defines a pair of positive integers $(a,b)$ to be a Oneful Pair, if $a+b+(a \cdot b) = 111$ 

For example, $(1,55)$ is a Oneful Pair, since $1+55+(1 \cdot 55)=56+55=111$.  

But $(1,56)$ is not a Oneful Pair, since $1+56+(1 \cdot 56) = 57+56=113$ not equal to $111$.  

Given two positive integers $a$ and $b$, output Yes if they are a Oneful Pair. And No otherwise.
practiceProblems.inputFormat: The only line of input contains two space-separated integers a and b.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: Output Yes, if (a,b) form a Oneful Pair. Output No if they do not.

practiceProblems.description:

It is already filled with X liters of water. \
Find the maximum amount of extra water in liters that Chef can fill in the bucket without overflowing.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Chef has a bucket having a capacity of K liters. \
It is already filled with X liters of water. \
Find the maximum amount of extra water in liters that Chef can fill in the bucket without overflowing.
practiceProblems.inputFormat: - The first and only line of each test case contains two space separated integers K and X - as mentioned in the problem.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, output in a single line, the amount of extra water in liters that Chef can fill in the bucket without overflowing.

sampleTestCases.explanation: The capacity of the bucket is 5 liters but it is already filled with 4 liters of water. Adding 1 more liter of water to the bucket fills it to (4+1)=5 liters. If we try to fill more water, it will overflow.

The capacity of the bucket is 15 liters but it is already filled with 6 liters of water. Adding 
9 more liters of water to the bucket fills it to (6+9)=15 liters. If we try to fill more water, it will overflow.

practiceProblems.title: Determine Cheaper TV Option - Debug The Code
practiceProblems.description:
Chef is looking to buy a TV and has shortlisted two models. \
The first one costs A rupees, while the second one costs B rupees. \
Since there is a huge sale coming up on Chefzon, Chef can get a flat discount of C rupees on the first TV, and a flat discount of D rupees on the second one. \
Help Chef determine which of the two TVs would be cheaper to buy during the sale.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Chef is looking to buy a TV and has shortlisted two models. \
The first one costs A rupees, while the second one costs B rupees. \
Since there is a huge sale coming up on Chefzon, Chef can get a flat discount of C rupees on the first TV, and a flat discount of D rupees on the second one. \
Help Chef determine which of the two TVs would be cheaper to buy during the sale.
practiceProblems.inputFormat: - The first and only line of each test case contains four space-separated integers A, B, C and D — the marked price (in rupees) of the first TV, the marked price (in rupees) of the second TV, the flat discount (in rupees) of the first TV, and the flat discount (in rupees) of the second TV.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, print a single line containing the string First if the first TV is cheaper to buy with discount, or Second if the second TV is cheaper to buy with discount. If both of them cost the same after discount, print Any.
